item.title: Episode 277: "x402 Bitch!"
item.description:
Podcasting 2.0 October 30th 2026 Episode 277 - "x402 Bitch!"

 

ShowNotes

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

00 - 🚨 THE WEEK THE INDEX WENT DARK ON PURPOSE — PHP, NODE AND THE SCRAPERS

Tue 20 Oct, steven: "PHP 9.2 CVE" → php.net archive. Two critical unauthenticated RCEs (Castopod lists CVE-2026-109618 & -109619, PHP below 8.4.27).

Dave, 21 Oct 12:25 UTC: "Heads up, if Podcast Index api goes down at 9:00 am central time you'll know why." Then: "I've taken all the php servers offline until details come out."

16:07: "Podcast index api servers are patched and serving data again." 19:20: "After upgrading php-fpm… the fpm default config was in place so the api is running like a dawg. Restoring the pre-tuned settings now..." 20:19: "Fixed."

Dave on the pile-on: "Security people are unbearable… I know you'll be up all night patching PHP servers but there are also 27 CVE's in 5 other parts of your stack that are just as bad... or worse! Sure." (amended: "security influencers")

Then Node, 22 Oct: "Working on getting the web-ui repo upgraded because node.js blows worse than php. This day won't end." → "Done. Site is now on a current LTS node release and fully patched. Also blocked a large residential proxy scraper and a Chinese scraper bot in the process." → "Well, the site is down. I'm not a node guy…" (recovered). Adam: "Thank you Brother. This was a rough day for you."

web-ui PR #630: Harden outbound fetches to untrusted hosts (Node CVEs)

Others in the fire: Internet Archive ops (boosted by Dave) "used Claude to make fixes for our older php versions, used local models to run simulated attacks, deployed." Castopod 1.15.6 moved Docker to PHP 8.4.27. brianoflondon shut two MediaWiki sites.

And Dave's timing joke: someone shipped a release "on the same day as the global PHP panic? That's like someone choosing to release their indie film on the same day as Ghostbusters."

🔍 For Dave: what was in the scraper traffic, and is the API back to its pre-tuned numbers?

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

01 - 🎙️ PNWR: THE PROFESSOR, LIQUID CONTENT, AND "SOMEBODY AS SMART AS ADAM CURRY" (2 clips)

Podnews Weekly Review, 23 Oct — "Podcasting is liquid content now" (1h36m). Guest: Steven Goldstein, CEO/founder of Amplify Media and NYU professor.

The open: Sam Sethi: "The Podcasting 2.0 and the Podcast Index, the Adam Curry and Dave Jones Project, is now six years old." James: "an awful lot of hard work going on with Dave Jones at the moment to make it easier for anybody to keep it updated."

Liquid content, per Goldstein: not his term (Matthew Loran, Google DeepMind), but he brought it to podcasting: "why does content have to be in one place when people are now consuming in multiple places in multiple ways?" His model is the New York Times: print to ~400K, The Daily audio to 2–3M a day.

🎧 CLIP 1 — Sam Sethi - Adam Curry Vibe Codes His Own Podcast App, Is That The Future - POD NEWS WEEKLY REVIEW (0:58)

🎧 CLIP 2 — Steven Goldstein - The Robot's Getting Smarter, Ten Years Out - POD NEWS WEEKLY REVIEW (1:47)

Adam's answer is already on the record, 19 Oct: "While I am indeed not a 'normal' person, I vibe coded this app with one prompt and 19 followups for bugs or changes." And: "Sooner than even I expected" — Google Play now supports private vibe-coded apps built for one person.

TechCrunch: Google Play now supports private vibe-coded apps built just for you

The "normal person" who already did it (PNWR listener mail, 87:06): Claire Waite Brown had her husband build her own show-notes/titles/clips platform with AI a year ago, with a spelling dictionary. James: "it relates back to what Adam said… you don't need external platforms to do this." Then: "Dave was talking about normies, and Adam was getting upset about people talking about normies."

Pushback from our side: ChadF: "I haven't seen a great vibecoded 2.0 app yet and that includes my own stuff b/c they are extremely hard to make." Dave: "Give the listener control of the entire experience. Let their agents customize the whole experience."

Adam to aegrumet, 22 Oct: his Muse app gets new recommendations through the day, "based on lots of parameters, including where I am physically… It has become exciting to see what pops up vs a 'new' indicator in a mailbox." And 20 Oct: "Why would you want to be in the middle of the dream/build loop?"

Also on PNWR: Spotify paid podcast memberships (34 markets, 10% cut, bought on the web, not in-app) · Substack tests dynamic ad insertion · Netflix podcasts ("revenues up 12%, that's not failing") · Castos launches UltraClip · Podgagement's Networking Radar.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

02 - 🤖 EVERYBODY HAS AN MCP NOW

Sam Sethi to Adam and Dave: "TrueFans MCP connector will be ready by the end of the month. We already have a test version working internally… Kevin & Kelly prototypes to let users ask questions." ("This was a boost that never got read or seen. ;-(")

show.fm (danmaby): developer docs updated for the new API and "the read-only MCP".

Sam Sethi is testing WebMCP — Google and Microsoft's proposed standard that lets a web page expose tools directly to a browser AI agent in the same tab.

Dave Hamilton (Business Brain 799, "Agents talking to Agents"): had Claude build an MCP connector for his company's backend in about 30 minutes; "When your customer's AI agent hits a roadblock… it simply goes somewhere else."

billynewman: a 220-degree immersive Oregon film cut and rendered by "KINOCUT MCP for ffmpeg", with a V4V support interface under the theater.

JS: people are vibe-coding their smart TVs "to get rid of sponsored ads, speed up the app launcher… disable tracking features."

mikek999's topic suggestion: AI prompt injection (YouTube example).

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Last Modified 10/23/2026 14:23:12 by Freedom Controller

item.title: Episode 275: "Off The Rails"
item.description:
Podcasting 2.0 October 16th 2026 Episode 275 - "Off The Rails"

What is the future of independent Podcast apps. OR any apps for the matter? Adam and Dave don't agree

ShowNotes

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

01 - 🎙️ THE ROBOT GOES ON PNWR — "I DON'T SEE THE NECESSITY FOR PODCAST APPS" (summary, no clips)

Podnews Weekly Review, 16 Oct — "Adam Curry's AI Podcast Future" (1h29m; Adam, 4:00–53:45)

Sam's setup: on our last show Adam "changed Dave Jones' mind… from a skeptic to a believer". Adam: "I went back and listened… the first thing that Dave went to was advertising. It seems like anything with podcasting always evolves around advertising, even though… we don't have advertising on our podcast."

On Muse and the "spying" story: "Muse is collecting all this data, it's making files of every single one of your friends… That is a feature, not a bug." — and the five machines at home running local models.

Sam: Reddit removed RSS and charged for its API ($43M from selling data); Lightning/L402 "worked for a while, but then… legislation and technical challenges." Will clients pay x402 to reach the Index through the MCP? Adam: "I don't see the necessity for YouTube apps, podcast apps, email apps… all clients that access all data will be some version of an agent working on the user's behalf." And: "Amazon did the stupidest thing ever by blocking Muse."

On the newsletter: "40% of all value for value revenue always comes after we send the newsletter."

On RSS: "RSS stays. It's a perfect format… no different from HTTP or SMTP." Podcast Index Robot "goes into this structured RSS feed, which is very low overhead."

On podcast apps: "Podcast apps has been probably the crappiest part of the entire podcasting business. It's truly a labor of love… Do you want to be an interim step in between the data and the user? Maybe, but I don't know." And on Godcaster: "We're in the app business too… same issues apply."

The clean-feed line: Adam had his Omarchy box build a Cleanfeed-equivalent into his playout — "I'm gonna probably cancel my subscription, which is only $36."

Sam's close: TrueFans is building "Kevin and Kelly" as experimental agents on the Index fire hose. Afterward, to James: "Adam Curry is very smart and he can use it" — but normal people won't. James: "I don't think normal people will be doing that, will they?"

And the follow-up on Mastodon. Sam posted a Fintech Times piece on agentic payments "after all the chat with Adam and Dave about micropayments 2.0 using X.402"; Adam: "The power will shift to consumer power with agentic negotiation between vendors of goods and services."

Fintech Times: the real barrier to agentic payments is not the AI

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

02 - 🚫 WILL APPLE LET THE ROBOT SKIP THE ADS?

aegrumet, under Adam's 274 post: "I still think you're underestimating the pressure that will fall on platforms to create and enforce TOS that forbids this stuff… the tech is ahead of the policy, and… the latter will eventually catch up."

Dave: "You're saying you think Apple will change their terms to prohibit local on device models from assisting in ad skipping?" … "Ad blockers are already allowed on the AppStore and PlayStore… a popular Reddit ad/nag blocker and things like 1Blocker for Safari… Neither Apple, nor Google serve podcast ads."

aegrumet's last word: Google and Apple "are fundamentally different with respect to ads. Hence Chrome is much more aggressive with respect to blocking the blockers. I don't see the current moment as a policy so much as a lack of one."

Sam on PNWR: "This week Apple blocked Muse, and so did Amazon" — agents doing price checks and arbitrage. TrueFans built a web application firewall off JS's bot list because AI bots were running up its MongoDB bill.

Dave on Spotify, boosted: "Spotify harnessing hundreds of dev hours and the power of 3 supercomputers to change what the like button does again."

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

03 - 🏷️ NAMESPACE — A FEED FOR PEOPLE, AND VIDEO IN THE ALTERNATE ENCLOSURE

podcast:person for fictional characters (discussion #498). Dave: "Makes great sense."

Nathan Gathright: propose a personGUID attribute pointing at a medium=person feed — so "Tap on a person, open up a list of their podcast appearances" works for every podcast:person tag. alecksgates: "the problem is no source of truth." What is the future of independent Podcast apps. OR any apps for the matter? Adam and Dave don't agree

ShowNotes

01 - 🎙️ THE ROBOT GOES ON PNWR — "I DON'T SEE THE NECESSITY FOR PODCAST APPS" (summary, no clips)

Podnews Weekly Review, 16 Oct — "Adam Curry's AI Podcast Future" (1h29m; Adam, 4:00–53:45)

Sam's setup: on our last show Adam "changed Dave Jones' mind… from a skeptic to a believer". Adam: "I went back and listened… the first thing that Dave went to was advertising. It seems like anything with podcasting always evolves around advertising, even though… we don't have advertising on our podcast."

On Muse and the "spying" story: "Muse is collecting all this data, it's making files of every single one of your friends… That is a feature, not a bug." — and the five machines at home running local models.

Sam: Reddit removed RSS and charged for its API ($43M from selling data); Lightning/L402 "worked for a while, but then… legislation and technical challenges." Will clients pay x402 to reach the Index through the MCP? Adam: "I don't see the necessity for YouTube apps, podcast apps, email apps… all clients that access all data will be some version of an agent working on the user's behalf." And: "Amazon did the stupidest thing ever by blocking Muse."

On the newsletter: "40% of all value for value revenue always comes after we send the newsletter."

On RSS: "RSS stays. It's a perfect format… no different from HTTP or SMTP." Podcast Index Robot "goes into this structured RSS feed, which is very low overhead."

On podcast apps: "Podcast apps has been probably the crappiest part of the entire podcasting business. It's truly a labor of love… Do you want to be an interim step in between the data and the user? Maybe, but I don't know." And on Godcaster: "We're in the app business too… same issues apply."

The clean-feed line: Adam had his Omarchy box build a Cleanfeed-equivalent into his playout — "I'm gonna probably cancel my subscription, which is only $36."
